extra.message: User-controlled input from request.form['expression'] is passed directly to eval() in the /evaluate route. This allows arbitrary Python code execution, e.g. submitting __import__('os').system('id') results in full remote code execution on the server.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: User-controlled input from request.form['address'] is concatenated into a shell command string ('nslookup ' + address) and executed via os.popen (rp). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters, e.g. '; cat /etc/passwd' or '$(id)', to execute arbitrary OS commands.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: User input from request.form['name'] is interpolated into a template string via Python string formatting and then rendered with render_template_string(). Because the attacker-controlled value becomes part of the Jinja2 template source, this is Server-Side Template Injection, allowing payloads like {{7*7}} or {{config}} / {{request.application.__globals__}} leading to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: User-supplied XML from request.form['xml'] is parsed with an lxml XMLParser configured with no_network=False and dtd_validation=True, which enables external entity and DTD processing. This allows XML External Entity (XXE) attacks to read local files (e.g. file:///etc/passwd) and perform SSRF via external network requests.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The result of eval(expression) (derived from user input request.form['expression']) is concatenated into an HTML response string returned directly without escaping. Even apart from code execution, this reflects attacker-controlled content into the page, enabling reflected Cross-Site Scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: User input request.form['address'] (via the command output) is reflected into the raw HTML response of the /lookup route without escaping, enabling reflected Cross-Site Scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The Flask secret_key used to sign session cookies is hardcoded ('Harry Potter And The Deathly Hallows'). Anyone with access to the source can forge/tamper with session cookies (e.g. set logged_in=True), bypassing authentication.

Flask debug mode is enabled (app.debug = True) and the app binds to 0.0.0.0. The Werkzeug debugger exposes an interactive console allowing arbitrary code execution on unhandled exceptions, and leaks stack traces / source code. This must never be enabled in production.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The 404 error handler passes the raw error object into the rendered template, potentially disclosing internal application/error details to clients.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: User registration stores the password from request.form['password'] directly into the database in cleartext (no hashing/salting). The login route at line 50 also compares the plaintext password. A database compromise exposes all user credentials.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: Sensitive functional routes (/evaluate, /lookup, /xml, /sayhi, /dashboard) perform no authentication or authorization check despite the application having a session-based login system. Any unauthenticated user can reach these dangerous endpoints (eval, command execution, XXE, SSTI), constituting missing authorization / broken access control.
